title: No-Knead Bread – Sourdough
description:
This No-Knead Sourdough Bread is made with your own homemade sourdough starter that rises overnight and is
baked the next morning. Or mix it up early in the morning and bake it at night. Up to you! A couple of my own
“cheating additions” – more rise and sharper tang – are noted in italics. All super easy and forgiving, have fun!
ingredients: 4 cups white bread flour, spooned and leveled (520 grams total flour)
1 tablespoon sea salt (16 grams; could be a little less if desired)
1/3 cup sourdough starter (90 grams) fed 4-10 hours earlier, using it slightly
after peaking (or a day or a few after feeding if refrigerated)
1-2 good pinches of instant or rapid-rise yeast (less than 1/4 teaspoon)
Feeding the Starter (Daily if on the Counter; Once a Week or So if in the Fridge); Mix as Well as You Can
½ cup (135 grams) of old starter (discard remainder if not using for baking)
directions: Put the flour in a good-sized bowl or pot, then mix in the salt and a good pinch or two of yeast (if you’re
making this without official starter, then use a full ¼ teaspoon of yeast).
Add starter and sour cream to a measuring cup and fill with water until 1 7/8 cups, stir to combine.
Pour starter-water into flour, incorporating everything using a strong (wooden) spoon. It should be a thick,
shaggy, heavy, sticky dough. Cover with a lid or wet kitchen towel and let rest 15 minutes or whenever.
With one hand (maybe wet), pull the dough from one side and stretch it upward, then fold it up and over to
the center of the dough. Turn the bowl and repeat, stretching and folding from the side, up over the
middle, repeat for about 30 seconds. Cover, rest, repeat the process 15 minutes later or whenever.
Proof overnight, at room temp. Cover with plastic wrap or lid (to keep the moisture in) and place on your
kitchen counter for 8-12 hours or longer. You can do the little folding thing whenever you feel like it.
The next day (or when nearly ready for baking), shape the dough a little and place it seam-side down on
parchment paper (maybe in a bowl) for final rising. It will still be pretty soft and shaggy, don’t worry. You
can put it in the refrigerator, and it will help with scoring the top before baking.
Fully heat the oven – with a lidded Dutch Oven or big Corning Ware dish inside – to 450F degrees.
When ready to bake, using a very sharp knife, lame, or razor blade, score the dough swiftly and deeply, at
a 45-degree angle, 3/4- 1-inch deep. One deep slash is just fine. Or criss-cross, or crescent shape. Oiling
the knife helps.
Carefully take out the hot Dutch Oven, gently lift your dough by holding the edges of the parchment and
place both bread and parchment directly into the pot.
Cover and bake (it’s ok if the parchment sticks out) for 30 minutes (or a little more with sour cream).
Remove lid (the bread should be puffed and just lightly golden) and continue baking 15 minutes (or a
little more) until deeply golden and internal temp reaches 202- 208F.
Remove bread from the pot and cool for an hour (if you can – it will smell heavenly!).
